nieuw.titel: Build each wizard around a clear, economical role
nieuw.tekst: Decide whether your wizard is a blaster, buffer or control piece, then tighten its build around that job. Aim to fulfil that role cheaply rather than taking the most expensive version.
nieuw.waarom: In his view, a cheaper, more clearly defined character improves your chances of winning through favourable points trades while leaving you options to pursue your plans.

nieuw.titel: Give a blaster mage multiple magic missiles
nieuw.tekst: Build a blaster mage with more than one magic missile. He recommends the Ruby Ring when you lack another option such as the Rod of the Damned.
nieuw.waarom: He says the double magic missile attack defines the blaster's role. Combining the Wood Elf missile with the Ruby Ring lets the caster choose different types of targets and remain effective.
nieuw.wanneerNiet: He notes that the Ruby Ring may fail to go off throughout a game, although in other games it works repeatedly.

nieuw.titel: Give blasters mobility to collect late-game points
nieuw.tekst: Give a blaster mage the mobility to find vulnerable targets, particularly a steed and, where available, movement in all directions. Use that reach to clear chaff and finish weakened or fragile units when late-game charges and combats no longer offer scoring opportunities.
nieuw.waarom: He finds lightly armoured, low-toughness skirmishers ideal missile targets, but their mobility makes reaching them important. He has seen a mobile blaster swing games by collecting extra points late.
nieuw.voorbeeld: In his High Elf game against Dark Elves, the opposing Pegasus-mounted wizard used Fireball and Pillar of Fire to collect about 300 points late, turning a likely narrow victory into a much larger one.
nieuw.wanneerNiet: He says rising Magic Resistance, especially Magic Resistance 2, and harder casting have made blasters less popular, although he still considers them worth considering for many armies.

nieuw.titel: Consider a Wood Elf blaster in Glade Riders
nieuw.tekst: He recommends a Wood Elf wizard with the Ruby Ring and Lore Familiar in a Glade Riders unit with Reserve Move as a strong blaster setup. Combine the Lore of the Wilds magic missile with the ring to address different targets.
nieuw.waarom: He considers the Lore of the Wilds missile exceptional and values the flexibility of using it alongside the Ruby Ring. Reserve Move supplies the move, cast and move again function he wants.

nieuw.titel: Use Reserve Move to cast and withdraw
nieuw.tekst: Use a Reserve Move unit to move a blaster into targeting range or out of enemy dispel range, cast, then move away again. He highlights this as a way to keep the wizard alive and protected within a unit.
nieuw.waarom: He values the ability to move, shoot and move again, together with the targeting protection the unit provides.
nieuw.voorbeeld: He points to a Bretonnian Exiles Outcast Wizard joining Mounted Yeomen as a cheap way to obtain this function.

nieuw.titel: Pair movement spells with combat buffs
nieuw.tekst: Consider a buff mage that combines a movement spell with a spell enhancing the unit's combat prospects. He highlights Arcane Urgency with Oaken Shield as one such pairing, aiming to arrange a fight heavily in your favour.
nieuw.waarom: He says movement and characteristic buffs shift the odds in your favour, and there are relatively few ways to stop buffing compared with the Magic Resistance that counters missiles.
nieuw.voorbeeld: He identifies Oaken Shield's inexpensive ward save as useful in Ogre Death Star builds.

nieuw.titel: Use movement debuffs to upset carefully judged ranges
nieuw.tekst: Use a control mage to disrupt enemy movement, including spells that reduce movement. He considers even Elementalism's minus-one-movement signature useful for interfering with carefully judged charge and missile ranges.
nieuw.waarom: In his view, movement is the source of the game's advantages. Good players operate as close as possible to the relevant range boundaries, making movement buffs or debuffs valuable.

nieuw.titel: Consider Necromancy to attack enemy leadership
nieuw.tekst: Consider Necromancy's leadership debuffs as a control tool. He particularly values the minus-two leadership effect for its potential to make critical leadership tests fail.
nieuw.waarom: He regards failing leadership tests as the next most important lever after movement: the effect may seem irrelevant until a decisive failure occurs.

nieuw.titel: Consider a Bone Dragon High Priest for control magic
nieuw.tekst: He considers a High Priest on a Necrolith Bone Dragon an ideal carrier for control magic because it can choose Illusion or Necromancy. Consider an Illusion setup with movement-disrupting and blocking spells, or Necromancy with Spirit Leech and other debuffs.
nieuw.waarom: He values the High Priest's access to both of these lores and the range of builds this gives Tomb Kings.

nieuw.titel: Use control spells to obstruct movement and charging lanes
nieuw.tekst: Look for control magic that blocks line of sight or creates dangerous or difficult terrain to interfere with enemy charges and movement. He regards forcing the opponent to take the low charge roll through terrain as an underused tool.
nieuw.waarom: He recalls the disruption Wood Elves could cause by blocking movement and charging lanes with Pillar of Fire and Tree Singing when those options were more effective.
